PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-07-08
55M, ambulatory visit for an annual check-up.

S:
Patient presents for a routine check-up. He reports feeling generally well with steady energy. Diet includes frequent sugary drinks, which was discussed. He works as a maintenance technician and stays active on the job. Sister with schizophrenia. Sleep is adequate and appetite is good. Lives with his spouse. Never smoker, rare alcohol. No new concerns today.

O:
BP 126/78, HR 72, RR 14, Temp 98.2 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 190 lb, BMI 28.
General: well appearing, in no acute distress.
HEENT: normal.
Neck: no lymphadenopathy, no thyromegaly.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Extremities: no edema, pulses intact.
Labs (prior week): Hgb 12.9 g/dL, A1c 6.1%, lipid panel within goal, basic metabolic panel normal.

A/P:
1. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks and adding regular walks and light strength work. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
2. Anemia, stable on recheck. Continue oral iron daily with vitamin C. Repeat CBC in 3 months.
3. Family history: reviewed relevant family history with patient and discussed reassurance and routine follow-up.
4. Health maintenance: colorectal screening discussed and scheduled. Influenza vaccine offered in the fall. Encouraged continued physical activity and balanced meals.
5. Lifestyle: reviewed portion sizes, limiting sugary drinks, and building regular activity into the workday. Discussed the value of consistent sleep and adequate hydration.

Return in 6 months to review labs, sooner as needed.
